title: DR1 tells the user who the consignment contact is and what they are responsible for; the frontend instead explains what selecting one does to the form.

finding.frontend: Under the heading the only line of guidance is "Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/copy/copy.en.js:4). It describes what the form does with the answer and never says who this person should be, so a trader with several saved addresses has nothing to choose on.
finding.prototype: DR1 answers the question the page is actually asking: "This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks." (app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:50-52). The same sentence is used in DR1's address book as the description of a branch address, so a trader meets one definition of the role wherever they meet it.
finding.difference: Replace the frontend hint with DR1's sentence, so the page says who the contact is rather than what the service does with the answer. Nothing else on the page changes.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any statement on the frontend contact page of who the contact is responsible to, or for how long.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs for fe-contact and dr1-contact-address-for-consignment and both copy sources; ran the falsifier by reading every line of body text on the frontend page between the heading and the buttons. It does not fire — the only guidance is the one hint, and the rest of the page is thirteen radios and the save actions. Checked the cross-reference claim: the same sentence is the branch-address hint at app/data/address-book-address-types.js:38, so a trader does meet one definition in both places. CORRECT.
finding.correction: Mis-cited, claim unaffected. The frontend hint was cited as copy.en.js:5; the hint is at :4 and :5 opens the errors object. The inline citation is corrected to :4; the evidence range :2-6 already covered it. Also noted but not raised here: DR1 puts an "Select an address" subheading above its radios and the frontend has none — that is a smaller copy difference on the same page and is left to a language pass rather than split into a second finding.
